title: PSA: Amazon’s 2026 Kindle back panels are popping off when owners remove their cases
summary: Taking off a protective case shouldn't double as a teardown.
body: TL;DR The removable back panels on the 2026 Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite can accidentally detach when removing a protective case. The issue occurs even with Amazon’s official cover, but hasn’t been observed on the aluminum Kindle or Paperwhite Signature Edition. Amazon says owners can simply press the panel back into place, although reassembly can cause alignment issues. We got our first hint that Amazon was preparing to make Kindle batteries easier to replace back in May, and the company delivered on that front with the launch of its redesigned Kindle lineup in October. It’s a welcome change for devices that people often keep for years, but some owners of the 2026 Kindle and Kindle Paperwhite are discovering that the removable back panel can come loose long before it’s time for a new battery. A Kindle owner on Reddit demonstrated how their Ube Kindle comes apart when removing a protective case. TikTok creator Jackie’s Book Tally shared a similar experience, showing how trying to peel away a clear case to put some stickers on the back of her Kindle causes the device’s housing to separate.

summary: The song became the longest No. 1, by run time, among other milestones.
body: “I was going through a bit of sad time,”  Taylor Swift told Jimmy Fallon in 2021 about the lyrics in “ All Too Well ,” which she cowrote with Liz Rose. “I started ad-libbing what I was going through and what I was feeling.” Originally released on Swift’s 2012 album Red , at just under five-and-a-half minutes in length, the song became the focus of her rerecorded Red (Taylor’s Version) , after growing into a beloved entry in her catalog among Swifties. Related Taylor Swift Sets New Grammy Record With 5 Years of Major-Category Nominations Taylor Swift Says Nashville Songwriters ‘Raised Me’ During Hall of Fame Induction Taylor Swift’s 13 Most Autumnal Songs (Led by ‘All Too Well,’ of Course) “All Too Well (Taylor’s Version)” launched at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated Nov. 27, 2021, as Red (Taylor’s Version) opened atop the Billboard 200 . Two versions made the set: one mirroring its original run time and a 10-minute, 13-second take (both of which combined into one listing on Billboard ’s charts). YouTube shows up in the Android Auto launcher when the car is parked. Along with this, Morphe’s version of YouTube and YouTube Music also get a host of playability improvements. Morphe is a popular open-source tool for modding popular Android apps to add features and remove ads from YouTube, YouTube Music, and other media streaming apps. In the last major update, it added 4K video downloads , surpassing download-quality limits even on the official YouTube app. Now, it’s out with another update that brings a host of changes to patched versions of Reddit, YouTube, and YouTube Music. One that truly stands out — and we hope isn’t blocked by Google — is the ability to play YouTube videos on Android Auto. Release notes for version 2.40 of the Morphe app say a new patch now lets Morphe YouTube be seen as a “parked video app.” As a result, the app shows up in Android Auto’s app drawer, and you can watch videos directly while your vehicle isn’t moving. title: Android just had one of its worst quarters, and Apple is benefiting
summary: Android just recorded its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, with Apple's iOS bucking the trend.
body: TL;DR Android accounted for 74% of global smartphone sales in Q3 2026, down five points from a year ago and its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, per Counterpoint Research. iOS climbed to a record Q3 share of 21% as iPhone sales grew year-on-year, even as the overall market shrank 16%. HarmonyOS held at 5% globally and took 22% of China’s market, with HUAWEI growing 12% while China’s market shrank 10%. The memory shortage has been dragging down phone sales all year, and new data shows it may be hurting Android more than its rivals. According to Counterpoint Research , global smartphone sales fell 16% year-on-year in Q3 2026, a sharper drop than the 11% decline seen in Q2. Android’s share of those sales slipped to 74%, down from 79% in Q3 2025. That’s the lowest share Android has ever posted in a third quarter, though it’s still a touch above the 72% it hit in Q4 2025, when new iPhones typically give Apple a seasonal bump.
